steps.title: What We Were Made For | Genesis 3:1-10
Icebreaker
paragraphs: When you were a child, where was your favorite hiding place?
When you want to get away from everything for a little while, where do you like to go?

steps.title: Small Group Introduction (Video)

steps.title: Introduction
paragraphs: From the beginning, God created people to live in His presence and walk with Him. But when Adam and Eve sinned, shame and fear led them to hide from the very One they needed most. Yet God did not abandon them. He came looking for them. Throughout Scripture, God makes His way toward people, and through Jesus He makes a way for us to be with Him again. As we begin Make Way, we are invited to walk closer with God and help others walk with Him.
What stood out to you most from this week’s message?

steps.title: Into the Word · Discussion 1
steps.question: What do these passages reveal about God’s desire to be with His people? How is walking in a relationship with God different from simply knowing about Him, and what might that look like in your everyday life?
steps.guidance: God made people for relationship with Him. Exodus 25:8 shows that His desire to dwell among His people continues beyond Eden. Help the group distinguish between religious knowledge or activity and a growing, daily walk with God.

steps.title: Into the Word · Discussion 2
steps.question: How do shame and fear affect Adam and Eve’s response to God? What are some ways we hide from God today, even when we know we need Him?
steps.guidance: The sermon traces the pattern of sin, shame, fear, hiding, and distance. Hiding may look like avoiding prayer, concealing sin, becoming self-reliant, or staying busy. Psalm 32 contrasts the burden of concealment with the freedom of confession. When we confess our sins to God and trusted others, we bring what was hidden into the light, where we can experience the freedom of God’s forgiveness, the peace of His grace, and the healing that comes through honest relationships.

steps.title: Into the Word · Discussion 3
steps.question: Why is it significant that God calls out to Adam after Adam has sinned? What do these passages reveal about God's heart toward those who are lost? How can guilt or shame keep us from returning to God, and how does knowing He pursues us change our response?
steps.guidance: Throughout Scripture, God takes the initiative to seek and restore those who are lost. God’s question, “Where are you?” invites Adam to respond; it is not a request for information. The shepherd’s search and the father’s welcome reveal His compassion and joy when sinners repent. Like the younger son, we may allow shame to convince us we are unworthy of God's love. Remind your group that we don't have to earn His love. Luke 19:10 tells us Jesus came to make way for us to be reconciled to God. Repentance means turning from sin and returning to the Father who welcomes us through Christ.
steps.instruction: Read Genesis 3:8–9, Luke 15:1–7, Luke 15:11–24, and Luke 19:10.

steps.title: Into the Word · Discussion 4
steps.question: How did sin change Adam and Eve’s relationship with God? How does Jesus make a way for us to be reconciled to God, and what difference should this make in how we approach Him today?
steps.guidance: Sin ruptured fellowship with God, but God did not stop pursuing His people. In Jesus, God came to dwell among us and demonstrated His love through Christ’s death for sinners. Restoration is a gift of grace, received through faith in Jesus, not something we earn by trying harder.

steps.title: Embrace and Embody
items: Remembering that we were created to walk with God.
Recognizing when sin, shame, or fear leads us to hide.
Responding to God’s invitation with honesty and repentance.
Resting in the grace He has shown us through Jesus.
Walking closer with Him and helping others walk with Him.

steps.title: Embrace and Embody · Question 1
paragraphs: As a group, discuss the following questions:

What is the difference between knowing about God and having a relationship with Him? How might the way we experience God's grace and pursue a closer relationship with Him influence the way we love, encourage, and help others walk with Jesus?

steps.title: Embrace and Embody · Question 2
paragraphs: What are some socially acceptable or even spiritually respectable ways we hide or avoid dealing with what God wants to address in our lives?

steps.title: Embrace and Embody · Question 3
paragraphs: What are some good things that can become substitutes for the relationship with God we were created to enjoy? How can we recognize when something good has become an unhealthy priority?

steps.title: Take Your Next Right Step
paragraphs: (Prayerfully consider one of the following next steps)
items: Seek God Daily: Set aside time this week to ask God, "Where am I spiritually, and what might You be inviting me to acknowledge or change?" Respond honestly through prayer.
Build Deep Relationships: Share with a trusted friend or group member one area where you want to walk more closely with God.
Live Generously: Make room in your schedule to be present with God and available to someone who needs encouragement.

steps.title: Closing Prayer
paragraphs: Heavenly Father, thank You for creating us to walk in relationship with You. Even when we turn away or try to hide, You lovingly pursue us. Help us to recognize the places where fear, shame, or distractions keep us from Your presence. Give us courage to draw near to You and make room for what You want to do in our lives. As we grow closer to You, use us to help others experience the hope of Jesus. May we be willing to make way for all You want to do in us and through us. In Jesus' name, Amen.

verses.text: Now the serpent was more subtle than any animal of the field which Yahweh God had made. He said to the woman, “Has God really said, ‘You shall not eat of any tree of the garden?’”
The woman said to the serpent, “We may eat fruit from the trees of the garden,
but not the fruit of the tree which is in the middle of the garden. God has said, ‘You shall not eat of it. You shall not touch it, lest you die.’”
The serpent said to the woman, “You won’t really die,
for God knows that in the day you eat it, your eyes will be opened, and you will be like God, knowing good and evil.”

When the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was a delight to the eyes, and that the tree was to be desired to make one wise, she took some of its fruit, and ate; and she gave some to her husband with her, and he ate it, too.
Their eyes were opened, and they both knew that they were naked. They sewed fig leaves together, and made coverings for themselves.
They heard Yahweh God’s voice walking in the garden in the cool of the day, and the man and his wife hid themselves from the presence of Yahweh God among the trees of the garden.

verses.text: Now all the tax collectors and sinners were coming close to him to hear him.
The Pharisees and the scribes murmured, saying, “This man welcomes sinners, and eats with them.”
He told them this parable.
“Which of you men, if you had one hundred sheep, and lost one of them, wouldn’t leave the ninety-nine in the wilderness, and go after the one that was lost, until he found it?
When he has found it, he carries it on his shoulders, rejoicing.
When he comes home, he calls together his friends and his neighbors, saying to them, ‘Rejoice with me, for I have found my sheep which was lost!’
I tell you that even so there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents, than over ninety-nine righteous people who need no repentance.

Luke 15:1-7.text:
Now all the tax collectors and sinners were coming close to him to hear him.
The Pharisees and the scribes murmured, saying, “This man welcomes sinners, and eats with them.”
He told them this parable.

“Which of you men, if you had one hundred sheep, and lost one of them, wouldn’t leave the ninety-nine in the wilderness, and go after the one that was lost, until he found it?


When he has found it, he carries it on his shoulders, rejoicing.


When he comes home, he calls together his friends and his neighbors, saying to them, ‘Rejoice with me, for I have found my sheep which was lost!’


I tell you that even so there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents, than over ninety-nine righteous people who need no repentance.

verses.text:
He said,
“A certain man had two sons.
The younger of them said to his father, ‘Father, give me my share of your property.’ He divided his livelihood between them.
Not many days after, the younger son gathered all of this together and traveled into a far country. There he wasted his property with riotous living.
When he had spent all of it, there arose a severe famine in that country, and he began to be in need.
He went and joined himself to one of the citizens of that country, and he sent him into his fields to feed pigs.
He wanted to fill his belly with the husks that the pigs ate, but no one gave him any.
But when he came to himself he said, ‘How many hired servants of my father’s have bread enough to spare, and I’m dying with hunger!
I will get up and go to my father, and will tell him, “Father, I have sinned against heaven, and in your sight.
I am no more worthy to be called your son. Make me as one of your hired servants.”’
“He arose, and came to his father. But while he was still far off, his father saw him, and was moved with compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.
The son said to him, ‘Father, I have sinned against heaven, and in your sight. I am no longer worthy to be called your son.’
“But the father said to his servants, ‘Bring out the best robe, and put it on him. Put a ring on his hand, and shoes on his feet.
Bring the fattened calf, kill it, and let us eat, and celebrate;
for this, my son, was dead, and is alive again. He was lost, and is found.’ They began to celebrate.
